message_1_subject: Exhibit C redline: tier split + true-up mechanism (NV-2041)
message_1_body:
Hi David,

Thanks for running through the draft earlier today. We attached a redline of Exhibit C and a short procurement summary that lays out the commercial intent. High level: Novum is asking for a flexible discount redistribution that lets us move unused committed units between adjacent tiers at quarter true-up with a small offset matrix to preserve vendor economics. Specific asks in the attached:

- Allow one intra-year redistribution per quarter true-up (max two per 12 months).
- Offset matrix to convert redistributed units to invoice credits rather than upfront refunds.
- Request a 30-day cash-equivalent escrow or a reserve that Redwood can debit to cover shortfalls during the first 3 billing cycles post-go-live.

We know this is non-standard; our procurement team wants to avoid large credit accruals while keeping usage flexibility. Deal: NV-2041.

Files: Novum-ExhibitC-Redline.pdf (redline), Procurement-Summary.xlsx (summary).

Can you confirm Redwood's stance on: (1) whether an escrow/reserve is acceptable (and if so what triggers release), and (2) whether the offset matrix can be implemented as invoice-credit logic vs. cash refunds?

If easier, we can hop on a 30-minute call tomorrow.

Best,
Elena
Procurement Partnerships
Novum Tech

message_2_subject: Re: Exhibit C redline: tier split + true-up mechanism (NV-2041)
message_2_body:
Elena — thanks for the redline and the clear summary. Looping in Neha (legal) and Marissa (AE) so we can table precise contract language and commercial impact. Quick reactions from my side:

- We like the intent of giving Novum flexibility across tiers, but we need a mechanism that caps our downside. Two controls we need to add: a minimum billable floor per quarter (to avoid 0s from repeated redistributions) and a hard cap on total credits across a 12-month window.
- Escrow vs reserve: we prefer an automatic invoice credit (simpler accounting) unless finance needs cash-held escrow for audit reasons. If Novum insists on cash escrow, we'll ask finance/treasury for the acceptable mechanics.
- Offset matrix: fine in principle. We need it expressed as a deterministic conversion table in the SOW so it can be automated. No open-ended manual credits.

Requested next items from Novum:
1) A short note confirming whether you can accept invoice-credit treatment (instead of cash escrow).
2) If escrow is required, specify the proposed triggers for release/return.
3) Any tolerance band (e.g., +/-10% usage variance) you expect to apply before a redistribution is allowed.

CC'd below is the portion of your email for context:

message_3_subject: Re: Exhibit C redline: suggested contract language (NV-2041)
message_3_body:
Elena / team — thanks for the draft. I reviewed the Exhibit C redline and propose the following contract edits to capture Redwood's commercial protections while honoring Novum's flexibility:

1) Redistribution allowance (new §2.3): "Customer may elect to redistribute up to [X]% of unused committed units to the immediately adjacent commitment tier at each quarterly true-up. Such redistribution may occur no more than twice in any rolling 12-month period."

2) Credit conversion (new §2.4): "Redistributed units shall convert to invoice credits using the conversion table in Annex A (the \"Conversion Table\"). Invoice credits are non-refundable and may be applied only against future Redwood invoices within twelve (12) months of issuance. In no event shall invoice credits be convertible to cash except as expressly agreed in writing by Redwood's finance team."

3) Floor and cap protections (new §2.5): "Each quarter shall have a Minimum Billable Floor equal to 75% of the preceding quarter's billable units unless otherwise mutually agreed in writing. Aggregate invoice credits issued in any consecutive twelve (12) month period shall be capped at 15% of the annualized committed spend under the Order Form."

4) Escrow / reserve alternative (new §2.6): "As an alternative to cash escrow, Customer may elect an automatic reserve mechanism (the \"Reserve\") whereby a percentage of monthly invoices is held as a credit balance on the Customer account. Redwood may apply the Reserve to cover immediate shortfalls during the initial three (3) billing cycles post-go-live. Release of any unused Reserve will occur upon the earlier of (a) the end of the third billing cycle, or (b) mutual written agreement."

Rationale: these edits preserve automation (invoice credits) while limiting financial exposure to Redwood. If Novum requires cash escrow for audit preferences, we'll need to scope the treasury/legal work and confirm acceptable mechanics — that'll take longer.

I attached a one-page Redline-suggestions.docx with in-line phrasing for your counsel. Happy to take a 30-minute call to walk through language. If Novum is comfortable with the Reserve mechanism, that will be our preferred path.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redline-suggestions.docx (attachment stub)

message_4_subject: Re: Exhibit C redline: suggested contract language (NV-2041)
message_4_body:
Neha / David — thanks for the fast turn. Reviewed Neha's proposed phrasing with our legal and procurement leads. A few points back to you: 

- Novum prefers invoice-credit treatment vs. cash escrow; we accept the Reserve mechanic as long as credits are available at the account level and apply automatically at true-up.
- The 75% floor is higher than we expected — would you consider 65% as a compromise? Our internal forecast smoothing assumes some seasonality.
- The 15% annual cap on credits is acceptable in principle; can Redwood confirm if that is calculated against ARR or the prior 12-month invoiced spend? We prefer prior 12-month invoiced spend.

We can take the rest to counsel, but we'd like to resolve the floor percent and credit-basis question before sharing a final DocuSign packet. I can turn around a short reply from procurement within 48 hours.

If helpful, here's a proposed one-pager summarizing the compromise: https://www.docusign.com/Envelope/ABC12345

Happy to jump on a quick alignment call — Marissa, are you available tomorrow 10–10:30 PST to walk the commercial tradeoffs?

Best,
